skill1: Activates when the shield created by Centi is destroyed. Affects all allies. Recovers 9.7% of the skill user's final Max HP as HP.

caveats: ⚑ Skill 2 has NO activation clause in the kit text, so its cadence is modeled as an interval trigger with an UNMEASURED 15 sec period. The kit states no cooldown; the whole shield/heal duty cycle rides on this guess.

⚑ 'Cooldown of Skill 2 ▼ 9.16%' is a PERCENT reduction, but the only schema stat is skillCooldownReductionSec (seconds). The 1.37 sec value is 9.16% of the guessed 15 sec base; both the base and the seconds conversion are unmeasured.

⚑ The kit states no duration and no stack cap for the Skill-2 cooldown reduction. Her RL lands a full charge every ~1.2-1.5 sec, so an uncapped permanent stack would drive the Skill-2 interval to zero; maxStacks 4 is an invented haircut, not a kit value.

⚑ The burst's DEF ▼ 14.54% is NOT modeled: the StatKey vocabulary has no enemy-DEF-reduction stat (defPct is self-DEF and documented inert; damageTakenPct is a different multiplier bucket and would land the effect in the wrong place). This is a REAL team-wide damage gain that the override currently drops.

⚑ The shield-destroyed heal is NOT modeled: its trigger (a Centi shield being BROKEN by damage) is unreachable at scope lock, where the boss deals no damage and shields only lapse by time. It is a cross-unit line (heal effects fire allies' 'recovery' triggers), so it is inert here but would matter against a damaging boss.
⚑ Burst flatDamage crit-eligibility left unset — deferred to the engine's global rider-crit behaviour rather than pinned per-unit; the kit text says nothing.

⚑ Base cadence (chargeFrames 60 / reloadFrames 111 / ammo 6) is datamined and known-unreliable; it sets the full-charge rate that drives the Skill-2 cooldown reduction, so a cadence error propagates straight into shield uptime.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Model: RL/Iron/Defender/Burst II shield-support. S1a 'Forcefully uses Skill 2' is encoded as a battleStart block carrying Skill 2's own payload (7% caster Max HP shield, 5 sec, all allies) so the t=0 forced cast is represented — the interval trigger on skill2 first fires at t=sec and would otherwise leave the opening uncovered. S1b keys off a chargeCounter{count:1} (fires on every full charge; the closest primitive to 'when landing a Full Charge attack' — at scope lock every RL shot lands, so land-vs-fire is equivalent) and grants a self skillCooldownReductionSec buff, which shortens interval-trigger timers, i.e. exactly the skill2 interval. S1c (heal on shield destruction) is unmodeled: its trigger cannot fire at scope lock. Burst is a burstCast flatDamage 145.46% of final ATK on the boss plus a self Max HP ▲5%/10 sec (targetMaxHpPct; kept per the HP/DEF-scaler rule even though she carries no atkOfMaxHpPct consumer). The burst DEF ▼ is unmodeled for lack of an enemy-DEF stat, not because it is inert. No noFb, no noRange, no core flags authored — burst-cast damage is engine-FB-exempt and riders are engine-force-noRange.

flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ case 2: a kit line with NO activation clause gets an invented trigger + cadence. Skill 2's prose states only the effect, never a cooldown. 15 sec is a mid-range defender-skill guess, nothing more; it sets the entire shield duty cycle (5 sec shield on a 15 sec period = ~33% uptime), which is what any shield-gated teammate (requiresShielded / 'shielded' trigger) reads.
flags.recipe: Datamine the Skill-2 cooldown for centi. Failing that, take a focus recording of centi in a team and count shield-application VFX over a 180 sec fight: period = 180/(applications-1), with the battle-start forced cast as application #1. Cross-check that the count exceeds 180/15 once full charges start landing (the S1b reduction shortens it).

flags.reasoning: The kit states a PERCENT reduction; the only available stat is skillCooldownReductionSec, denominated in seconds. The conversion therefore inherits the guessed 15 sec base — if the real base is 20 sec the value is 1.83, if 10 sec it is 0.92. Percent-vs-seconds is also a semantic mismatch: the kit line most likely cuts the REMAINING cooldown per proc rather than granting a standing seconds-off buff, and the schema has no primitive for a one-shot cooldown pulse.
flags.recipe: Pin the Skill-2 base cooldown first (same recipe as above), then measure the EFFECTIVE shield period in a recording where centi is landing full charges continuously vs one where she is not (e.g. stunned / reloading-heavy opening). The delta in shield applications per minute gives the real per-charge reduction directly, without needing the percent-to-seconds fiction.

flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ case 4 (stack/currency steady-state). The kit states neither a duration nor a cap. Her charge economy — chargeFrames 60, ammo 6, reloadFrames 111 — lands roughly one full charge per 1.2-1.5 sec, i.e. ~10 per 15 sec window, so an uncapped permanent stack collapses the Skill-2 interval to zero within seconds and would give ~100% shield uptime. 4 stacks (~5.5 sec off a 15 sec base -> ~9.5 sec effective) is a deliberately conservative haircut chosen to avoid that degenerate case; it is NOT derived from the kit.
flags.recipe: Measure the effective shield period at steady state (mid-fight, after her charge cadence has stabilised) from a focus recording. effectiveInterval = base x (1 - 0.0916 x observedStacks) gives the real stack count; if the measured period is at or near the game's skill-cooldown floor, the correct model is a clamp rather than a stack cap.

flags.estimate: unmodeled — worth roughly a low-single-digit % team damage gain while active
flags.reasoning: A boss DEF reduction acts on the flat DEF subtraction in the damage formula, which is a different mechanic from damageTakenPct (a multiplier-bucket term). The StatKey list has no enemy-DEF stat, and defPct is documented as self-DEF and inert. Encoding it as damageTakenPct would reproduce roughly the right direction in the wrong bucket and would compose incorrectly with any other Damage-Taken source — the exact fudge the measured>fudge rule forbids. It is dropped honestly instead.
flags.recipe: Needs an engine primitive (an enemy-DEF-down stat feeding the boss-DEF subtraction) before it can be modeled. Sizing: run the existing boss-DEF sensitivity path with DEF reduced 14.54% for 10 sec per centi burst and diff total team damage; that bounds the cost of the omission without changing any shipped value.

flags.estimate: unmodeled — inert at scope lock, non-inert against a damaging boss
flags.reasoning: The trigger is shield DESTRUCTION (broken by incoming damage), not shield EXPIRY. At scope lock the boss deals no damage and nothing breaks a shield, so the line can never fire; modeling it on a 5 sec expiry timer would invent a trigger the kit does not state and would spam allies' 'recovery' triggers (an on-recovery consumer such as a heal-synergy teammate would then get free uptime). Skipped on TRIGGER inexpressibility, explicitly not on the 'heals do nothing' isolation reasoning the hard rules forbid.
flags.recipe: Only becomes measurable in a fight where the boss actually damages the team. If a shield-break trigger is ever added, the block is heal{} -> target allies on that trigger; until then the correct record is unmodeled + this flag.

flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ case 1: datamined cadence fields are known-unreliable, and here they are load-bearing beyond raw DPS — the full-charge rate is the trigger frequency for the Skill-2 cooldown reduction, so a cadence error propagates directly into shield uptime and therefore into any shield-gated teammate.
flags.recipe: Frame-count one magazine from a focus recording: charge-start to release for chargeFrames, last-shot to first-shot-of-next-magazine for reloadFrames, and count shots per magazine for ammo. Compare against data/ before trusting the derived charge rate.

flags.reasoning: The kit text says nothing about critical hits on the burst damage, and the schema notes a global rider-crit behaviour that already decides this class of hit. Authoring crit:true or crit:false per-unit here would pin a behaviour on no evidence and could diverge from the roster-wide convention.
flags.recipe: Read burst popups in a centi focus recording: orange + crit icon on the burst number means it crits. If it does and the engine default is off, pin crit:true; a single clean recording settles it.
